QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_31

question.text: Mr. Arjun Desai (SIA) is engaged by Navya Agritech — a Section-8 FPE serving 50,000 smallholder farmers — to certify impact for the Annual Impact Report. The management has NO existing impact framework. Which first step is MOST appropriate?

answer.text: Immediately apply IRIS+ metrics without further discussion
Co-develop a Theory of Change with the SE to map inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, impact and assumptions, then select IRIS+/GRI indicators that map to the ToC
Issue the Annual Impact Report based on management self-assessment only
Decline the engagement because no framework exists

explanation.text: The Logic: Best practice per Ch 6: begin with a Theory of Change that maps causal pathways and assumptions, then overlay IRIS+ / GRI / SDG indicators that fit. Picking indicators before ToC is 'tail wagging the dog' and risks missing material outcomes or including irrelevant metrics. The Trap: Option A skips the diagnostic step. Option C outsources the assurance to management and defeats SIA independence. Option D abandons the client unnecessarily — ToC co-development is exactly the SIA's role-add. Cross-Exam Context: ToC approach is covered in XXIII Ch 5 and reinforced in Ch 6 — SIAs are expected to use ToC as an anchor for every engagement regardless of the SE's starting maturity. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Bill the ToC workshop as a separate pre-engagement deliverable — it both improves the quality of your subsequent evidence work and prevents scope-creep disputes when the audit field work starts.
